entries.text: Florida regulates three kinds of in-home provider under Chapter 400, Part III: licensed home health agencies, licensed nurse registries, and registered homemaker/companion service providers.
entries.src: Florida AHCA; Florida Statutes ch. 400 Part III

entries.text: A nurse registry arranges contracts for nurses, aides, homemakers and companions who work as independent contractors, and needs its own AHCA licence (s. 400.506).
entries.src: Florida AHCA, Nurse Registries; s. 400.506 F.S.
entries.note: Caregiver Bench recruits W-2 employees for licensed agencies and places nobody as a contractor. Whether that activity needs any licence is a legal question: get the lawyer's written answer. This is not legal advice.

entries.text: Anyone providing homemaker or companion services must register with AHCA; the registration costs $50.75 for two years and every employee needs background screening. An agency that already holds a home health or nurse registry licence does not need the separate registration.
entries.src: Florida AHCA, Homemaker and Companion Services FAQ; s. 400.509 F.S.

entries.text: Senate Bill 1068 (2026) would add client disclosures and naming and licence-display rules for nurse registries, with 1 July 2026 as its effective date. The Senate page read here showed it at committee stage; a secondary site describes it as in force.
entries.note: Whether it became law was not confirmed on the official site.

entries.text: Florida counts from the Home Care Association of Florida: 6,056 in-home providers in total = 1,154 licensed-only home health agencies + 1,151 Medicare/Medicaid-certified home health agencies + 1,197 nurse registries + 2,554 homemaker and companion service providers.
entries.src: Home Care Association of Florida, "2024 Year in Review"
entries.date: document covers 2024; publication date not shown (probably early 2025)
entries.note: What the count includes: every licence or registration type under Florida Statutes ch. 400 Part III. What it does not tell you: how many are active, how many are private pay, how many are in Tampa Bay, or how many caregivers each employs. Nurse registries refer independent contractors and are not W-2 employers, so they are not Caregiver Bench customers. The association cites no external source; the AHCA facility search is the authority and has not been counted here.

entries.text: Home health and personal care aides held about 4,677,100 US jobs in 2025. Employment is projected to grow 18% from 2025 to 2035 (about +847,300 jobs), with about 760,500 openings a year. Median pay was $17.21 an hour ($35,800 a year) in May 2025.
entries.src: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Outlook Handbook
entries.date: page last modified 27 Aug 2026 · forecast period 2025–2035 · pay as of May 2025
entries.note: Definition: SOC 31-1120, home health aides and personal care aides together, all employers and payers (Medicaid, Medicare, private pay), whole United States. It is not a Florida or private-pay number. "Openings" include replacing people who leave the occupation, not only new jobs.

entries.text: Previous edition, kept for comparison only: about 4,347,700 jobs in 2024; projected growth 17% from 2024 to 2034 (about +739,800 jobs); about 765,800 openings a year; median pay $16.78 an hour in May 2024.
entries.src: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Occupational Outlook Handbook (2024–34 edition)
entries.date: forecast period 2024–2034 · pay as of May 2024 · superseded
entries.note: Superseded by the 2025–35 edition. Do not quote it as current. Same definition (SOC 31-1120).

entries.text: Median caregiver turnover was 75.5% in 2025, after a peak of 79.2% in 2023.
entries.src: 2026 Activated Insights Benchmarking Report, as cited by HHAeXchange
entries.note: Read through a secondary article. The report itself was not opened.

entries.text: Indeed is a top-two caregiver source for 43.3% of agencies, employee referrals for 15.9%. Agencies whose best source is their own website report the lowest turnover (65.8%).
entries.src: 2026 Activated Insights Benchmarking Report, as cited by HHAeXchange

entries.text: Agencies paying $15–17.99 an hour report median turnover of 84.4%; at $18–19.99 it is 53.0%.
entries.src: 2026 Activated Insights Benchmarking Report, as cited by HHAeXchange
entries.note: Secondary citation. Pay is set by the agency, not by a recruiter: a limit on what recruiting alone can fix.

entries.text: Roughly four in five caregivers who leave do so within their first 100 days.
entries.src: Activated Insights, as cited by several vendor blogs
entries.note: Vendor blog citing the report; wording varies between sources.

entries.text: CareerPlug: applicant-tracking software for home care, the official ATS partner of the Home Care Association of America, used by large franchise brands; integrates with myCNAjobs.
entries.note: Software the agency runs itself. Pricing not found.

entries.text: myCNAjobs: a job network built for caregivers, CNAs and HHAs; says it reaches 5.2 million caregivers.
entries.note: The reach figure is a vendor claim.

entries.text: Augusta: caregiver-recruiting software for home care that matches applicants to agencies and publishes a national recruiting benchmark (120,000+ applicants in Q1 2026); says it has helped hundreds of agencies.
entries.note: Closest to "more applicants reach an interview". Still software, not a done-for-you service with a guarantee. Pricing not found.

entries.text: Hellohire: a recruiting assistant for home care that engages and screens candidates and schedules interviews. Apploi and Hireology: recruiting/ATS platforms used in long-term care and multi-location providers.
entries.note: Third-party descriptions; none of these sites was tested.

entries.text: Home care deal-making rose in 2025: 104 announced or completed transactions, up about 40% on 2024; private equity did 43 of them (11 new platforms, 32 add-ons). Personal home care attracted the largest pool of investors.
entries.src: Capstone Partners, Home Care Sector Update
entries.note: An investment bank that sells M&A advice: the counts are its own tally.

entries.text: Q2 2026: eight non-medical home care deals closed, including General Atlantic's $3 billion purchase of TEAM Services Group. Q1 2026: 22 home-based care transactions closed across all segments.
entries.src: Home Health Care News and Axial, both citing Mertz Taggart quarterly reports
entries.note: National figures. No Florida or Tampa Bay deal data was found.

entries.text: Examples of buyers rolling up personal care agencies: Avid Health at Home (backed by Havencrest) announced its eighth acquisition in 2026; Care Advantage is listed with 16 acquisitions.
entries.src: Home Health Care News; Owler company listing
entries.note: Why it matters to you: buyers pay for agencies that can staff their hours. It does not show that any buyer wants a recruiting company.

plan: How many private-pay agencies are there in Tampa Bay, and how big are they?
partly
Statewide counts found (reported). The local, private-pay number is unknown: your own list (875) is the best figure and is not verified against AHCA.
What do owners say their biggest staffing problem is?
open
Published reports say turnover and early exits. Your own calls: 0 owner conversations. Only your calls can answer this for your market.
Who already sells caregiver recruiting to agencies, and how?
partly
One national done-for-you recruiter found (Carework), several software tools, job boards and marketing agencies. Prices are mostly not public. No Tampa Bay-local recruiter was searched for.
What do agencies pay today for hiring help, and what would they pay?
open
No pricing was found for any competitor. Ask owners; note every answer as a "willingness to pay" market note.
How large is the private-pay home care market?
open
Market-size reports are behind a paywall (IBISWorld). Unknown.
Which rules limit what Caregiver Bench may do in Florida?
partly
Provider types and the nurse-registry definition read on official pages. The answer for a recruiting-only company needs the lawyer.
Is the caregiver shortage getting better or worse?
answered
BLS 2025–35 edition: +18% jobs and about 760,500 openings a year nationally. Still getting tighter.

comp.note: Built from six web searches on one day. Not finding a competitor here is not proof that none exists: Florida-local recruiters, staffing firms, Facebook groups and LinkedIn were not searched. Everything in "what they say" is the company's own claim unless marked.
cats: Direct competitors: someone else does the caregiver recruiting for the agency
Possible partners and routes to owners

items.name: Carework
items.what: Done-for-you caregiver recruiting: posts the job ads, calls, texts, screens and schedules applicants; says its team works 7 days a week so every applicant gets a same-day reply. Also sells a hiring course (HireEd) and runs a podcast.
items.who: Home care agencies across the US
items.diff: Works the agency's own applicants from job ads. You promise caregivers who actually work, with a show-up and 90-day guarantee, and you take no money per placement of a client.
items.evid: Recommended by Stephen Tweed; resource partner of the Home Care CEO Forum. No published results found.

items.name: Well Beyond Care
items.what: Launched a caregiver recruitment and management service for organisations in 2021, sold monthly.
items.who: Assisted living, senior housing, private duty agencies
items.diff: Unknown whether the service still runs.

items.name: A remote recruiter hired directly by the agency
items.what: Agencies advertise for offshore recruiters with home care experience to do 15–20 candidate screenings a week.
items.who: Agencies that want an in-house assistant
items.pos: Cheap labour the owner manages himself
items.diff: The owner must train and manage the person. You sell the result, not the hours.
items.evid: One job advert seen; how common this is, is unknown.

items.name: CareerPlug
items.what: Applicant-tracking software; official ATS of the Home Care Association of America; integrates with myCNAjobs.
items.evid: Customer quotes on its own site.

items.name: 100Hires
items.what: Recruiting software for home care: sorts applicants and books interviews.
items.pos: A recruiting tool priced for an agency
items.diff: Same: a tool, the agency does the work.
items.evid: Its own percentage claims; no source given.

items.name: Augusta
items.what: Caregiver recruiting software built for home care; automates outreach; integrates with scheduling systems.
items.pos: Automate the grunt work of recruiting
items.diff: A tool, with a support team from the industry.

items.name: Agency management systems (AxisCare, WellSky, AlayaCare, CareSmartz360, ShiftCare)
items.what: Scheduling, billing and visit verification; some add hiring features.
items.pos: Run the whole agency in one system
items.price: ShiftCare lists from $9 per staff a month; a third-party page says AxisCare starts around $200 a month (not confirmed by AxisCare)
items.diff: Not competitors for recruiting. They are where the owner's data lives and a possible integration later.

items.name: myCNAjobs
items.what: Caregiver job board and network; sold as a subscription, monthly or yearly.
items.pos: Calls itself the nation's largest network of care workers
items.diff: A source of applicants. Somebody still has to answer them fast.

items.name: Indeed
items.what: General job board; the top source of applicants for many agencies.
items.price: Pay per posting or per application
items.diff: A source. Your library data: Indeed is a top-two source for about 43% of agencies.
items.evid: Activated Insights data already in your library.

items.name: Care.com
items.what: Marketplace where families hire caregivers directly, without an agency.
items.price: Family membership about $39.99 a month (a review site's figure)
items.diff: Competes with your customers for caregivers, not with you.

items.name: Nurse registries (Florida)
items.diff: Different legal model (contractors). You stay W-2 recruiting for licensed agencies.

items.name: General staffing firms
items.evid: No search done: this is a gap, not a finding.

items.name: Approved Senior Network (ASN)
items.what: Marketing agency for home care since 2008: SEO, ads, social, CRM, referral marketing, sales training; also advises on recruiting.
items.who: Home care and senior care businesses, US and Canada
items.diff: Sells client leads first; recruiting is a side service.

items.name: Home Care Marketing Pros
items.what: Family-owned agency in Bradenton, Florida (founded 2016): websites, SEO, ads; says it helps hire caregivers too.
items.who: Home care and home health providers
items.diff: A Florida firm already talking to your owners. Possible partner or competitor.
items.evid: Listed in the HCAOA vendor directory.

items.name: Sagapixel
items.what: SEO and Google Ads for home care.
items.price: Says its Google Ads campaigns cost $90–150 per client lead
items.diff: Client leads, not caregivers who work.

items.name: ChoiceLocal
items.pos: Says more than 1,000 private-pay agencies use it
items.diff: Shows that private-pay owners do buy outside services at scale.
items.evid: Its own claim in the HCAOA directory.

items.name: Home Care CEO Forum (Stephen Tweed)
items.what: Peer groups of agency owners; names "Resource Partners" it recommends to members.
items.diff: A route to owners that Carework already uses.

items.name: HCAOA and HCAF
items.what: National and Florida trade associations with vendor directories and partner programmes.
items.diff: A listing puts you next to competitors in front of owners.

items.name: Software marketplaces (CareerPlug, JazzHR)
items.what: Marketplaces where recruiting add-ons and agencies are listed.
items.pos: Distribution inside a tool the owner already pays for
items.diff: Later-stage route; needs a product that plugs in.
